factCards.text: Double-entry bookkeeping records every amount twice, once as a debit and once as a credit, so the two sides of the ledger always agree. The method was first described in print by Luca Pacioli in 1494.
Precious metals are weighed in troy ounces of about 31.1 grams, noticeably heavier than the ordinary ounce of about 28.35 grams.
factCards.sourceTitle: The Royal Mint — Troy weight explained

factCards.text: Coins in everyday circulation are generally struck from base-metal alloys such as cupronickel or plated steel, so the metal in them is worth less than the figure stamped on the face.
